Referral Note (primary care)

Ms. Harmon, a 26-year-old woman, is referred for psychiatric evaluation after multiple emergency department visits for suicidal thoughts, each following conflict in her relationships. She reports rapid changes in mood that she cannot explain and difficulty coping when upset, and she has worked only intermittently. Depression was diagnosed at age 19; she has had two psychiatric hospitalizations for suicidal ideation and a history of self-injury. She is not currently taking any medication. Medical history is notable for migraine headaches. Reports occasional binge alcohol use. Referred for diagnostic evaluation and treatment recommendations.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Casually dressed; appropriately groomed. Long sleeves.

Behavior: Alert and cooperative. Tearful throughout the interview. Checks her phone several times during the interview.

Speech: Normal rate, volume, and tone.

Mood / Affect: Mood "all over the place." Affect labile.

Thought / Perception: Thought processes logical. Denies hallucinations. Denies current suicidal intent.

Cognition / Insight: Alert. Insight fair; judgment impulsive during emotional distress.
